topic: Integrated Digital Design of Efficacy and Optimal Treatment of Oral Drugs
title: Integrated Digital Design of Efficacy and Optimal Treatment of Oral Drugs
session_title: Meet the Industry Candidates Poster Session: Process & Product Development and Manufacturing in Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals
abstract: The formulation of orally solid dosage forms is crucial for the pharmaceutical industry as it significantly impacts drug performance. Formulation factors, including tablet porosity, granules porosity, excipient composition, and particle size distribution (PSD) of granules and active pharmaceutical ingredient (API), affect oral bioavailability. 1,2 Manufacturers develop various drug formulations to control release and enhance bioavailability (drug efficacy) during drug development. Predictive dissolution modeling is commonly applied to support early-stage formulation design and manufacture process development, enabling the identification of critical material attributes (CMAs) of tablets without extensive laboratory dissolution testing. 3 Population balance model (PBM) is widely applied for tablet dissolution modeling due to their moderate computational cost and preserved interpretability compared with physics-based simulations (such as discrete element method) and data-driven methods. Current PBM-based dissolution models can predict dissolution behavior based on material properties such as size distribution, API solubility, and tablet porosity. 4 However, most existing models are tailored for direct compression tablets. There is a lack of PBM models capable of predicting dissolution for tablets produced from granules, despite granulation being commonly used in tablet manufacturing to enhance flowability, compressibility, and content uniformity. 5 In this work, we proposed a population balance model with semi-empirical breakage kernels to simulate the disintegration and dissolution of solid oral doses (tablets) comprised of granules and direction compression tablets. This model was trained and validated using acetaminophen tablets manufactured from dry granulation line under varying conditions of crystal size distribution (CSD), granule size distribution (GSD), tablet porosity and granules porosity as well as tablets produced from direct compression. This model demonstrates accurate capture of dissolution profile. Sensitivity analysis was conducted to identify the relative importance of material properties and assess model uncertainty. Additionally, we integrated our dissolution model with physiologically based pharmacodynamic-pharmacokinetic (PDPK) modeling for drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and elimination (ADME). This combined approach allows prediction of plasma concentration profiles based on formulation properties. Our in-silico studies demonstrate the impact of dissolution and disintegration on drug plasma concentration, illustrating the potential applications for rational formulation design and optimal dose regimen application. "Optimizing oral bioavailability in drug discovery: an overview of design and testing strategies and formulation options." Journal of pharmaceutical sciences 106.4 (2017): 921-929. 2. Fasinu, Pius, et al. "Diverse approaches for the enhancement of oral drug bioavailability." Biopharmaceutics & drug disposition 32.4 (2011): 185-209 3. Zaborenko, Nikolay, et al. "First-principles and empirical approaches to predicting in vitro dissolution for pharmaceutical formulation and process development and for product release testing." The AAPS journal 21 (2019): 1-20. 4. Matsunami, Kensaku, et al. "Mathematical models of dissolution testing: Challenges and opportunities toward real-time release testing." International Journal of Pharmaceutics (2024): 125002. 5. Shanmugam, Srinivasan. "Granulation techniques and technologies: recent progresses." BioImpacts: BI 5.1 (2015): 55.
